The presence of marked, thick-walled enhancement ('Enhancement Quality': 'Marked', 'Thickness of enhancing margin': '>3mm') and a significant necrotic core ('Proportion Necrosis': 19.41) are classic radiological hallmarks of glioblastoma, which is the most common IDH-wildtype glioma. In the context of diffuse gliomas, radiologically evident necrosis, typically seen as a non-enhancing core surrounded by contrast enhancement, is the defining feature of a CNS WHO grade 4 lesion. The 'Marked' 'Enhancement Quality' and thick enhancing margin further support this conclusion. There are no features suggestive of a lower-grade (2 or 3) tumor.

overall_comment: The combination of advanced patient age (68 years) and classic imaging features of a solitary temporal lobe mass with marked, thick-walled enhancement and a large necrotic core provides a high-confidence prediction for Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
